dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a packaged graph model, this projection returns its second component: the function assigning a natural-number degree to a vertex and graph.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the quantity inside the vertexwise inequality the packaged model's degree, which for the concrete package is the ordinary graph degree.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a packaged graph model, this projection returns its first component: a measure on simple graphs with vertex set Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the outer real-valued measure in the conclusion the graph law stored in the concrete package.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n and p in [0,1], this constructs a graph model whose law is the binomial random-simple-graph measure on Fin n with parameter p and whose vertex statistic is ordinary graph degree.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies the probability space in the conclusion as the binomial random graph on n labeled vertices with edge parameter p(n), and identifies the tested statistic as each vertex degree.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the n- and p-indexed package type that holds a measure on simple graphs together with a degree-like function from a vertex and graph to a natural number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It packages the two semantically relevant components later selected by LocalDef001 and LocalDef002; the indices n and p fix the graph size and parameter.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor builds a LocalDef004 package from a graph measure and a natural-number-valued vertex statistic.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It confirms that the two projected components are precisely the graph law and degree function supplied by LocalDef003.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every finite vertex type Fin n, vertex v, and simple graph G, the subtype of neighbors of v is finite.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the finiteness needed to form the ordinary finite graph degree appearing in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the division operation from a division-inverse monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the real numbers it supplies the division used in the constant 9/10.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Eventually
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate holds eventually along a filter when the set of points satisfying it belongs to that filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Used with the natural-number atTop filter, it turns both the growth assumption and probability conclusion into assertions valid for all sufficiently large n.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.atTop
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a preorder, atTop is the filter generated by upper intervals [a, infinity).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: On Nat, eventuality means that there is a threshold N after which the stated predicate holds for every n >= N.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices strictly below n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the labeled vertex set of every graph, and the conclusion quantifies over every vertex v in Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: GE.ge
dependency_coverage.meaning: The expression a >= b is defined as b <= a.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the conclusion require that the real-valued graph-event measure is at least 9/10.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the heterogeneous addition operation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real arguments it forms the coefficient 2*C + 5 in the degree threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the heterogeneous division operation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real arguments it interprets 9/10 as real division, hence as the real number 0.9.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the heterogeneous multiplication operation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real arguments it forms (n-1)*p(n), C*log n, 2*C, and (2*C+5)*log n.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the heterogeneous subtraction operation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With natural-number arguments it forms n-1 before casting to Real, so subtraction is truncated at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the non-strict order relation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it expresses C >= 0, the eventual bound (n-1)p(n) <= C log n, and, through GE.ge, the probability lower bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This invokes the strict order relation selected by the relevant typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it requires every vertex degree, after casting, to be strictly less than (2*C+5) log n.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure mu and set s, this is the real number obtained by applying mu to s and converting the resulting extended nonnegative value to Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It represents the real-valued mass, and here the probability, of the event that all vertex degrees satisfy the strict threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: Membership.mem
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the membership relation supplied by a Membership instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses that each p(n) lies in the closed interval [0,1] and also participates in the set-based definitions used by eventuality and neighbor sets.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers, including zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.cast
dependency_coverage.meaning: This maps a natural number into a type with a natural-number cast, here Real.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This establishes the numeral-construction side condition that a successor n+1 is at least two when n is nonzero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is elaboration support for the real numerals 2, 5, 9, and 10 and adds no mathematical hypothesis to the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instNeZeroSucc
dependency_coverage.meaning: This establishes that every natural-number successor is nonzero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports construction of the displayed numerals and adds no quantified condition or restriction to the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instPreorder

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the atTop filter, so sufficiently large means sufficiently large in the usual natural-number order.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number literal in a type carrying the corresponding OfNat instance.

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1
dependency_coverage.meaning: This derives interpretation of the numeral 1 from a type's distinguished one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real it supplies the upper endpoint 1 of [0,1].

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of p's values after subtype projection, of C, of logarithms and bounds, and of the converted graph-event probability.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary addition on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the coefficient expression 2*C + 5 its usual real-arithmetic meaning.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the standard multiplicative, inverse, and division structure on Real.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the usual non-strict order on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the usual strict order on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary multiplication on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard embedding of natural numbers into the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the real number one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the upper endpoint in the requirement p(n) in [0,1].

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instPreorder
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard preorder induced by the usual order on Real.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.log
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the real natural logarithm, extended by the displayed definition so that log(0)=0; on positive natural inputs it is the ordinary natural logarithm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies log n in both the assumed upper bound on (n-1)p(n) and the conclusion's degree threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: Set
dependency_coverage.meaning: A set of elements of a type is represented by its membership predicate.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.Elem

dependency_coverage.name: Set.Icc
dependency_coverage.meaning: Set.Icc a b is the closed interval consisting of x with a <= x and x <= b.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.instMembership

dependency_coverage.name: SimpleGraph

dependency_coverage.name: SimpleGraph.instMeasurableSpace

dependency_coverage.name: Subtype.val
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the underlying value from an element of a subtype.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This derives interpretation of the numeral 0 from a type's distinguished zero.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatAtLeastTwo

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets every natural-number literal as itself in Nat.

dependency_coverage.meaning: This is natural-number subtraction, which truncates at zero.

dependency_coverage.meaning: This forms a set from the predicate characterizing its elements.

dependency_coverage.meaning: This chooses a finite enumeration structure for a type already known to be finite.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of measures on a measurable space.

dependency_coverage.name: SimpleGraph.binomialRandom
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a vertex type V and p in [0,1], this is the binomial random-simple-graph measure obtained from the Bernoulli law on admissible unordered, non-diagonal edges via the graph edge-set map.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For V=Fin n and p=p(n), it is the random graph law under which the all-degrees-below-threshold event has probability at least 9/10.

dependency_coverage.name: SimpleGraph.degree
dependency_coverage.meaning: The degree of vertex v in G is the cardinality of its finite neighbor set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the conclusion a uniform bound on the ordinary degrees of all vertices, equivalently a strict upper bound on maximum degree.

dependency_coverage.name: SimpleGraph.neighborSet
dependency_coverage.meaning: The neighbor set of v in G is the set of vertices w adjacent to v.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its finite cardinality is the degree tested for every vertex in the graph event.

dependency_coverage.name: Finite
dependency_coverage.meaning: Finite alpha is the proposition that the type alpha has finitely many elements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to each neighbor subtype, it justifies converting that subtype to a Fintype so its cardinality and hence graph degree are defined.

dependency_coverage.name: Subtype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A subtype consists of elements satisfying a specified predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It represents both parameters p(n) constrained to [0,1] and neighbor sets as types of vertices satisfying membership predicates.

binders: p is an arbitrary sequence indexed by natural numbers, with each p(n) a real number in the closed interval [0,1].
C is an arbitrary real number.
hC is a proof that C is nonnegative.
hbound is a proof that, for all sufficiently large natural numbers n, (n-1)*p(n) <= C*log n, where n-1 is natural-number subtraction before being cast to Real.
hypotheses: There exists N0 such that for every natural n >= N0, the real inequality (n-1)*p(n) <= C*log n holds.
conclusions: There exists N1 such that for every natural n >= N1, under the binomial random-simple-graph law on vertex set Fin n with edge parameter p(n), the event that every vertex v has degree strictly less than (2*C+5)*log n has real-valued probability at least 9/10.
mathematical_definitions: Eventually atTop on Nat means for all sufficiently large natural numbers.
Fin n is the labeled vertex set {0,1,...,n-1}.
The concrete graph law is SimpleGraph.binomialRandom (Fin n) p(n), the binomial random-simple-graph measure obtained from Bernoulli choices on admissible unordered edges.
The degree of v is the number of vertices adjacent to v.
The measured event is {G : every v in Fin n satisfies degree_G(v) < (2*C+5)*log n}; equivalently, all vertex degrees, and hence the maximum degree when vertices exist, obey that strict bound.
Measure.real converts the event's extended-nonnegative measure to a real number; for this probability law it is the event probability.
The logarithm is the real natural logarithm; on positive n it is the usual log n, while the supplied definition sets log 0 = 0.
Natural subtraction is truncated, so the factor n-1 is zero at n=0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every sequence of probabilities p(n) in [0,1] and every nonnegative real constant C, if (n-1)p(n) is at most C log n for all sufficiently large n, then for all sufficiently large n a binomial random simple graph on n labeled vertices with edge probability p(n) has probability at least 0.9 of having every vertex degree strictly below (2C+5) log n.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Both the premise and conclusion are asymptotic eventual statements, so the proposition imposes no requirement at any fixed finite collection of small n.
The edge parameter may vary arbitrarily with n; it is not a single fixed probability.
The premise bounds (n-1)p(n), not n*p(n), and uses natural subtraction before the cast to Real.
The degree threshold is strict: degree_G(v) < (2*C+5)*log n, not <= that quantity.
The conclusion is a fixed probability lower bound of 9/10; it does not assert convergence of that probability to one or give a quantitative rate in n.
The implication is vacuous for any chosen p and C for which the eventual growth hypothesis fails.
At n=0 the vertexwise event is vacuous and log 0 and n-1 are both zero, but eventuality permits all such small-n behavior to be discarded.
The statement concerns simple graphs on exactly Fin n and the ordinary degree of every vertex; it does not state analogous bounds for other graph models, subgraphs, or average degree.
The proposition does not encode an explicit cutoff N or any dependence of that cutoff on p and C.
